from google.cloud import kms_v1
from google.cloud import storage

def envelope_encrypt(bucket_name, blob_name, plaintext):
    # Initialize KMS client
    client = kms_v1.KeyManagementServiceClient()
    
    # Set up resource names
    project_id = "your-project-id"
    location_id = "global"
    key_ring_id = "your-key-ring-id"
    crypto_key_id = "your-crypto-key-id"
    key_name = client.crypto_key_path(project_id, location_id, key_ring_id, crypto_key_id)
    
    # Create a client for Cloud Storage
    storage_client = storage.Client()
    bucket = storage_client.bucket(bucket_name)
    blob = bucket.blob(blob_name)
    
    # Generate data encryption key (DEK)
    dek = os.urandom(32)
    
    # Encrypt the data encryption key (DEK) using the key service (envelope)
    response = client.encrypt(request={"name": key_name, "plaintext": dek})
    encrypted_dek = response.ciphertext
    
    # Encrypt the data (plaintext) using the data encryption key (DEK)
    encrypted_data = encrypt_data(plaintext, dek)
    
    # Store the encrypted data and encrypted DEK in the blob
    blob.upload_from_string(encrypted_data + encrypted_dek)
    
    return blob_name

def encrypt_data(plaintext, key):
    # Implement your data encryption logic using the provided key
    # For example, using AES encryption:
    cipher = AES.new(key, AES.MODE_EAX)
    ciphertext, tag = cipher.encrypt_and_digest(plaintext.encode('utf-8'))
    return ciphertext

def main():
    bucket_name = "your-bucket-name"
    blob_name = "your-blob-name"
    plaintext = "Your sensitive data here"
    
    encrypted_blob_name = envelope_encrypt(bucket_name, blob_name, plaintext)
    print(f"Encrypted blob stored at {encrypted_blob_name}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
